title: A Billion-Dollar Cocaine Ship
central_question: Record Busts, 1: smugglers craned a billion dollars of cocaine onto a cargo ship; Hamburg found 16 tonnes in tins of wall filler; Ecuador found nearly 22 tonnes under a pigsty. Which was the worst hiding spot?
content_notes: Tone: deadpan about the schemes (a ship's own crane, tins of wall filler, a pigsty); the joke is on the smugglers, never on anyone harmed, and no victim, user or animal suffering is shown (the pigs are calm and unhurt). The eight Gayane crew members pleaded guilty (prison sentences followed): the plea is stated, they are never named and appear ONLY as dark rim-lit silhouettes tagged NOT A LIKENESS. The shipping line was not accused of any wrongdoing: it is not named on screen, and the ship, containers and crane carry no logo, livery, name or number. The Hamburg recipient (arrested Feb 2021) and the Vinces caretaker (arrested Jan 2024) are ACCUSED only: never named, 'arrested' with 'prosecutors say' / 'accused' on screen, AS OF OCT 2026; the Dutch man is a silhouette, the caretaker is not drawn. Coast Guard, customs, police and soldiers are generic figures with no badge, flag, patch or insignia; no weapon is drawn, nobody is struck, the only contact is hands behind the back. The freight papers, tins and sacks carry only our own typed words (no real document, label or brand imitated). The deck, the mess room, the Hamburg shed, the Dutch street and the Ecuadorian farm are illustrations, not the reported places. Every card is our own typed graphic. No dialogue or quotation card. Facts verified 2026-10-21.

lines.text: Smugglers loaded a ship with a billion in cocaine.
Its own crew craned it up from speedboats.
Then a swab found cocaine on the second mate's hands.
Hamburg customs found 16 tonnes in wall-filler tins.
The name on the paperwork? Arrested.
Ecuador's army raided a pig farm.
Under the pig pens, they found nearly 22 tonnes.
Then customs seized the ship itself.

claims.text: On 17 June 2019 at the Packer Marine Terminal, Port of Philadelphia, U.S. Customs and Border Protection with federal, state and local partners found cocaine worth more than $1 billion (CBP's estimate: about $1.3 billion street value) in seven shipping containers aboard the container ship MSC Gayane. Narration: 'Smugglers loaded a ship with a billion in cocaine.' Headline 'A BILLION-DOLLAR / COCAINE SHIP'. The shipping line was not accused of wrongdoing and is not named on screen.

Prosecutors say crew members loaded bulk packages of cocaine onto the ship at sea from speedboats that approached in the middle of the night, hoisted the cargo nets aboard with the ship's crane, hid the drugs among legitimate cargo in containers and resealed them with fake seals. Narration: 'Its own crew craned it up from speedboats.' Callout 'THE SHIP'S OWN CRANE'.

Coast Guard officials swabbed crew members for cocaine residue and found it on the hands and arms of the ship's second mate, according to his arrest affidavit; he told investigators he had been paid about $50,000 for his part. Narration: 'Then a swab found cocaine on the second mate's hands.' Label 'PHILADELPHIA · 17 JUNE 2019' with the sub 'Coast Guard swab test (arrest affidavit)'. The second mate later pleaded guilty and was sentenced; never named, silhouette.

Eight crew members of the MSC Gayane, including the chief mate and the second mate, pleaded guilty to conspiracy charges in federal court in Philadelphia; prison sentences followed (the fourth engineer, for example, 5 years 10 months in April 2021). Label '8 CREW PLEADED GUILTY' with the sub 'Federal court, Philadelphia (DOJ)'.

STATISTIC (counter): CBP's final figure was 39,525 lb of cocaine (nearly 20 US tons, about 17.9 metric tonnes) from seven containers, the largest cocaine seizure in CBP's 230-year history (first reported as about 16.5 tons / 33,000 lb). Counter '39,525 LB' with the label 'CBP'S BIGGEST COCAINE BUST EVER'.

Hamburg, February 2021: acting on a Dutch risk analysis, German customs checked containers shipped from Paraguay on 12 February and found 16,174 kg (about 16 tonnes) of cocaine hidden in 1,728 tins of construction putty / wall filler; German customs called it the largest amount of cocaine ever seized in Europe. Narration: 'Hamburg customs found 16 tonnes in wall-filler tins.' Label 'GERMAN CUSTOMS · HAMBURG · FEB 2021'.

The freight document for the Hamburg containers was addressed to a 28-year-old man in Vlaardingen, the Netherlands, registered as the recipient, who was arrested on 24 February 2021, Dutch prosecutors said. Accused only, never named, no outcome found AS OF OCT 2026. Narration: 'The name on the paperwork? Arrested.' Label 'ARRESTED, PROSECUTORS SAY' with the sub 'Accused only (AP, Reuters)'.

FUN FACT: tracing the same recipient, Belgian customs found 7.2 more tonnes of cocaine in Antwerp, hidden in a container of wooden blocks from Panama; with Hamburg, more than 23 tonnes, reported as Europe's biggest cocaine haul. Card 'SAME CASE, ANTWERP: / 7.2 MORE TONNES / IN WOODEN BLOCKS'.

Vinces, Los Ríos province, Ecuador, Sunday 21 January 2024: more than 150 soldiers raided a farm during the state of emergency's military offensive, after military intelligence work. Narration: 'And the biggest?' (editorial rehook) / 'Ecuador's army raided a pig farm.' Label 'VINCES, ECUADOR · 21 JAN 2024'.

The cocaine was stored in underground stashes built beneath a pig shed on the farm: close to 22 tonnes by the army's count (21.5 tonnes at the destruction days later), the largest drug seizure in Ecuador's history. Narration: 'Under the pig pens, they found nearly 22 tonnes.' Label 'ECUADOR'S BIGGEST DRUG BUST'.
One man, the farm's caretaker, was arrested at the scene and ordered held in pretrial detention; accused only, never named or drawn. Label sub 'One arrest: the caretaker, accused'.

On 4 July 2019 CBP executed a seizure warrant and seized the MSC Gayane itself, which CBP called the largest vessel seized in its 230-year history (the ship was later released on bond; the shipping line was not accused). Narration: 'Then customs seized the ship itself.'
